text:
sec-alert-bot: :warning: Suspicious runtime activity detected on node ip-10-2-5-77. Pod default/cache-worker-77 shows hostPath to /etc, hostNetwork=true, and additional caps. Image digest mismatch with registry.

natalie: which pod exactly? can someone paste the pod yaml?

sec-alert-bot: pod: default/cache-worker-77
kubectl get pod cache-worker-77 -n default -o yaml
```
metadata:
  name: cache-worker-77
  namespace: default
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  serviceAccountName: cache-sa
  containers:
  - name: cache
    image: registry.internal/redwood/cache@sha256:bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
    securityContext:
      capabilities:
        add: ["SYS_ADMIN"]
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /host-etc
      name: host-etc
  volumes:
  - name: host-etc
    hostPath:
      path: /etc/hosts-secrets
```

omar: bad combo. hostPath -> /etc/hosts-secrets is sensitive. That image digest doesn't match the one pushed earlier. check RBAC: any new clusterrolebindings for cache-sa?

natalie: running `kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.subjects[*].name}\n' | grep cache-sa || true`
result: `crb-cache-sa-olm cache-sa` created at 1841234455 -> bound to cluster-admin

tony: escalate: someone probably created a binding then spun up this pod with elevated caps. Immediate actions: cordon node, delete pod, revoke SA tokens, remove CRB.

oncall: cordoning node ip-10-2-5-77 now `kubectl cordon ip-10-2-5-77` -> ✅

oncall: deleting pod `kubectl delete pod cache-worker-77 -n default --grace-period=0 --force` -> ✅

ben: collecting artifacts: grabbing kube-apiserver audit logs, admission controller logs, and the node's kubelet journal. Uploading to secure bucket s3://redwood-secure/incidents/1841234567/.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline change detected: pipeline 'cache-service' had a step at 1841234400 that pushed registry.internal/redwood/cache@sha256:aaaaaaaa... subsequent push at 1841234460 introduced unsigned digest bbbbbbbb... cosign verify FAILED for bbbbbbbb.

natalie: remove clusterrolebinding: `kubectl delete clusterrolebinding crb-cache-sa-olm` -> in progress. Also rotating KMS key referenced by secrets used by cache service. Key id: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/service-keys/cryptoKeys/cache-enc.

tony: block the unsigned image in the registry and create an allowlist for signed digests. Deploy-bot can enforce image policy cluster-wide.

deploy-bot: image enforcement: flagged tag 'cache:latest' and digest bbbbbbbb as blocked. Mutating webhook updated to deny unsigned images.

omar: action checklist (short):
- node cordoned and pod removed (done)
- CRB deleted and SA tokens revoked (in progress)
- KMS key rotation triggered and secrets rewrapped (in progress)
- registry audit and rollback any deployments using that digest (assigned to infra)
- rebuild node from golden image and validate host integrity (next)
- rotate service TLS certs and any long-lived tokens (next)

ben: note: I pulled the kubelet journal and found a suspicious exec into container at 1841234442: `nsenter --target 1 --mount --uts --ipc --net` — suggests possible escape attempt. Adding to timeline.

natalie: communications: post initial incident note to #incidents and ping SOC. Drafting short blurb for legal/compliance. Need to capture scope: any other namespaces using cache-sa?`kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.serviceAccountName=="cache-sa") | {ns:.metadata.namespace, name:.metadata.name}'`

infra-bot: found 2 other pods using cache-sa in staging namespace created ~1841234505. They have since been evicted.

tony: containment complete for now. Next: forensic image of node and rebuild. Also run clusterwide RBAC audit script and schedule postmortem. Assign owners: natalie (incident lead), omar (containment + RBAC), ben (forensics), infra (registry + rebuild).

sec-alert-bot: marking incident severity P1 and creating ticket SEC-1841234567.

natalie: good work. keep chatter limited to channel. we'll brief execs after initial triage.

ben: uploaded logs + cosign outputs + kubelet journal to s3://redwood-secure/incidents/1841234567/artifacts/ and set retention 365d.

deploy-bot: policy: disabled service account token automount for cache service deployments cluster-wide via patch to admission config.

omar: final note for now: rotate cluster bootstrap tokens and run KMS key access review. we'll reconvene 30m.
